title: the librarian's memory is four row-addressed tables — nodes, lists, links, blobs — each row VOID, NOTCACHED or DATA under a gen
intention: The trees tool holds the Q#108 schema (outline 4.3.1.5.1.6): nodes, lists, links and blobs, each row addressed by node_address (T1, a90747de35d2), carrying a gen and one of three states; reads take a Ref and a stale gen reads Gone; void walks the node's in list; a link is one row held by both endpoints' lists; deposit returns a node address and the node's in list holds the leaf back; meta holds provenance and standing, and confidence is absent until scored.
why: Akien, Q#108 (2026-11-14, outline 4.3.1.5.1.6): 'nodes have to be fast, really fast. row ids are fastest. for lists of anything, we should stick with row ids.' Q#104 (4.3.1.5.1.2): a node id is its master row number, never a search. Confidence ruled absent until scored (orchestrator, 2026-11-14): an invented default is an unmeasured claim wearing a measurement's clothes (Law 3).
traces_to: Law 1 (every pointer a direct row fetch); Law 3 (confidence absent until measured); Law 7 (a stale ref reads loud Gone, never the new tenant).
how: Re-scope of the seed branch ticket-06db-row-ids @94da6412d onto T1's codec. D1: four tables cairn_mem_nodes/lists/links/blobs (row bigint PK = row half of the address, gen int, state CHECK, nodes kind/payload/blob/meta jsonb/out/in/seq; lists owner/items bigint[]/weights real[]/next; links a/b/weight/traversals; blobs kind/bytes), with row CHECKs (state one of three; DATA node has payload or blob; VOID row data cleared; weights length = items length). D2: write/read/void per table; read(Ref) raises Gone on gen mismatch; void bumps gen, walks `in`, removes itself from each source's `out`, clears data. Gap rows NOTCACHED, read-through via injected master-fetch, lowest-VOID reuse and injected home-reserver kept from the seed. D3: link(a,b,w) one link row whose address joins a.out and b.in; linked(); traverse bumps traversals. D4: lists chain to `next` past a chunk size. D5: a payload past the inline size goes to a blob, node.blob its address. D6: seq from one sequence, moved on every node write. D7: deposit/deposit_keyed return a node address; the leaf stores it, and the node's `in` list holds the leaf's address back (leaf addressing per outline 4.3.1.5.1.6.6: each leaf table gains an additive row bigint column and keeps leaf_id; its table tag is assigned at its birth by an injected tag-registry callable the home librarian answers, from 0x0100 upward; tags.json pins only the core four). D8: meta carries provenance and standing; confidence is never written by deposit. D9: dedup through librarian_content_index pending Q#109. D10: repoint test_a_node_without_an_embedding_is_found_by_its_key and every in-tool caller of node_id_for/link_id_for; node_id_for deleted. Migration moves out to T5.

clauses.claim: deposit into a scratch leaf returns a node address whose tag is nodes and whose row reads DATA with kind and payload; the leaf row stores that address, and the node's in list holds the leaf's address; the leaf table carries an additive row bigint column beside leaf_id, and its tag came from the injected tag registry, 0x0100 or above
a write at row 123 into a node table whose last row is 12 lays rows 13..122 NOTCACHED and row 123 DATA; a read of row 50 with a master-fetch returns the master's data and leaves row 50 DATA locally

void(a) removes a from the out list of every source named in a's in list, leaves the row VOID with data cleared and gen bumped; read(Ref(a, old gen)) raises Gone, never the next tenant's data; the next home reserve hands that row back before any new row
on a remote box (CAIRN_HOME_HOST set) reserve asks the injected home-reserver and never mints a row; with none given it refuses naming the home host, and nothing lands

a state outside VOID/NOTCACHED/DATA, a DATA node with neither payload nor blob, a VOID row still holding data, and a list whose weights length differs from its items, are each refused by the table CHECK and by the write door, naming the field
link(a, b, w) writes exactly one link row; its address is in a's out list and b's in list; traverse bumps traversals on that one row; linked(a) and linked(b) both name it
a list past one chunk chains through next and reads back as one ordered sequence of addresses with its weights parallel
a payload past the inline size lands in a blob of the given kind, the node's blob names its address and its payload is empty, and reading the node returns the bytes
seq strictly increases across every node write, void included, so a reader asking for rows past seq s gets exactly the rows written after s
a freshly deposited node's meta carries provenance and standing and has no confidence key, and the node reads as 'unscored'; no write path fills a default
the same content deposited twice, into two trees, lands one node row (found through librarian_content_index) and two leaves, and the second deposit appends an attestation (held on Q#109)
test_a_node_without_an_embedding_is_found_by_its_key runs green over the address API, and no name node_id_for remains in the trees tool

decisions.text: D1-D9: the four tables, their CHECKs and doors, Ref/Gone, void-walks-in, links, list chains, blobs, seq, deposit returning an address with the leaf back-pointer, meta without a confidence default, dedup via the content index.
D10: repoint the sibling proof to the address API.
The red-first proof, one tooth per clause, over store.scratch tables only (rewritten from the seed's 7 teeth).
The seed's migrate_to_row_ids.py leaves this ticket (it moves to T5, re-shaped to the four tables); this ticket deletes it from the branch.

out: cairn/devices/librarian device code and proofs, block reservation and bus verbs (d32faaf16223, T3)
every tree-search change (nearest/route/neighbors keep walking leaf embeddings, Q#110)

measured.saw: the seed branch @94da6412d: row ids, three states, gap fill, read-through, lowest-VOID reuse and injected reserver 7/7 green; test_a_node_without_an_embedding_is_found_by_its_key 4 red on node_id_for; leaf tables key leaves by text leaf_id, so a leaf has no row to address yet
measured.how: bin/cairn test over both proofs on akiendelllinux; read of _LEAF_COLUMNS in trees.py

measured.saw: Q#109, Q#110 and Q#111 answered by Akien; leaf addresses settled as a CC mechanism at outline 4.3.1.5.1.6.6
